review: The test still requires a public target-marking action, so it cannot pass through a generic aim fallback.
It verifies no immediate damage at confirmation, a projectile in flight after the opponent turn, later damage, and preservation of the player turn.
Reflection is limited to completing the AI-owned opponent turn in this isolated simulation fixture; production callers do not depend on the private method.
The target was corrected to the opponent's actual fixture position so the assertion measures the intended marked impact rather than a miss outside the blast radius.
result: No user behavior constraint was weakened.
